title: A recursive upper bound for multicolour Ramsey numbers
statement:
Fix an integer $m \ge 1$ of colours and integers $k_1, k_2, \dots, k_m$ with $k_i \ge 2$ for every $i$, and let $r(k_1, \dots, k_m)$ denote the multicolour Ramsey number: the least $n$ such that every colouring of the edges of the complete graph $K_n$ with $m$ colours contains, for some colour $i$, a complete subgraph on $k_i$ vertices all of whose edges have colour $i$. Then
\[
r(k_1, \dots, k_m) + m \;\le\; \sum_{i=1}^{m} r(k_1, \dots, k_{i-1}, \, k_i - 1, \, k_{i+1}, \dots, k_m) \;+\; 2,
\]
where the $i$th summand is obtained from $r(k_1, \dots, k_m)$ by decreasing the argument $k_i$ by one.
hypotheses_covered: c is a function Fin m → ℕ giving the m target clique sizes
